## The Nearly Horizontal Blast at Mount St. Helens

In the two months before May 18, 1980, Mount St. Helens experienced earthquakes and small explosions. On May 18, the volcano’s steep north flank fell in a landslide, triggering a blast that traveled nearly horizontally. A powerful vertical eruption followed.

The blast developed into a gravity-driven flow of hot material. It felled millions of trees, stripped bark and branches, and scraped away soil in places.
